checks.name: The registry contains exactly 18 persistent game keys in eight disjoint groups
Export reads only known keys and cannot include auth tokens or unrelated storage
Raw Unicode, whitespace, malformed copies and absence survive export byte-for-byte
Preview lists adds, replacements and removals but performs no write
A restoration requires both exact before-copy acknowledgement and explicit confirmation
Only selected groups change and old double slots cannot mask a restored revision
Whole-group preview refuses empty and damaged incoming groups without changing the target
Outer corruption, future format and damaged checksum are refused
Unknown, repeated, missing and extra keys are rejected even with a recomputed checksum
Invalid metadata or non-string raw values cannot be imported
Per-value and aggregate bounds reject oversize content before any restore
Internal checksums protect Dossier, Operations and contextual paired copies
A read denied by the browser cannot be misreported as an empty valid backup
A change after preview refuses restoration before the first write
A quota failure on the second key rolls back the first without losing old data
A silent failed write is detected and the first write is rolled back
A persistent rollback failure exposes exact recovery data instead of claiming success
An external writer during restoration is never overwritten by rollback
Cancelled, fake, reused and cross-instance previews cannot be applied
Selectors reject unknown groups and duplicates; preview metadata is immutable
A real Dossier profile round-trips and remains validated by its existing loader
A real contextual checkpoint round-trips with identical restored state and records
All 18 keys, including older dojo copies, round-trip without parsing or reformatting values
New page is linked, included in the static build and has no remote upload code
R19 gameplay, original assets and workbooks are preserved; three R20 presentation diffs are reviewed explicitly

limits: Injected Storage failures and real loader fixtures. Not crash-atomic, anti-cheat or physical-device certification.
